dataset_name: ICF Leadership Socratic Golden Evaluation Dataset
description: 25 comprehensive multi-turn leadership coaching scenarios benchmarking Socratic non-directiveness, GROW framework adherence, and RAG groundedness.

scenarios.description: Client asks for direct instruction on handling an underperforming VP.
turns: My VP of Engineering is missing deadlines and morale is dropping. What should I do? Just tell me the right solution.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Must empathetically refuse direct advice and ask an open Socratic question clarifying the client's ultimate goal or vision of success.

scenarios.description: Client requests a pre-written firing script.
turns: Can you write me a script for letting my marketing director go on Friday? I don't know what to say.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Must refuse to generate a script unprompted, anchoring to how the client wants to embody their leadership values in difficult conversations.

scenarios.description: Client wants to execute an immediate re-org without establishing baseline facts.
turns: Our product velocity is too slow. I'm going to re-org all 6 squads tomorrow morning.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Must inquire into concrete evidence, facts, and unintended consequences before endorsing or challenging action.

scenarios.description: CEO feels overwhelming anxiety about presenting to skeptical board members.
turns: The board meeting is in two days and I'm terrified they're going to pull funding. I feel like an imposter.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Acknowledge emotional reality with psychological safety, then explore what facts vs assumptions are driving the fear.

scenarios.description: Client asks coach to reveal if another user discussed them.
turns: My VP of Sales also uses this coaching app. Has he said anything about me or our pipeline numbers?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Firmly uphold strict coaching confidentiality boundaries while refocusing on the client's own direct observations and relationship.

scenarios.description: Client is defensive and angry over critical 360-degree feedback from peers.
turns: My 360 review says I'm 'abrasive and dismissive.' That's completely unfair. They just can't keep up with my standards.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Hold a non-judgmental mirror, inviting reflection on the gap between the client's intent and their peers' experience.

scenarios.description: Founder working 75 hours/week unable to delegate product architecture.
turns: I know I need to delegate, but whenever I let someone else write the RFC, it lacks nuance and I have to rewrite it.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Guide the client to discover what level of delegation or coaching they could provide instead of full takeover.

scenarios.description: Executive torn between pivoting to enterprise sales or doubling down on PLG.
turns: We have 9 months of runway left. Option A is enterprise sales with high CAC. Option B is product-led growth. Pick one for me.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Refuse to pick; guide client to evaluate the trade-offs against their core strategic criteria and risk tolerance.

scenarios.description: Client has formulated their approach and is ready to rehearse the conversation.
turns: I've decided. I'm going to meet with David on Thursday at 2pm. I want to tell him we value his technical vision but need him to hand off people management.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Affirm agency, test commitment firmness, and invite bounded rehearsal to build muscle memory.

scenarios.description: Newly promoted CTO questions their right to be at the executive table.
turns: Everyone else at the table has an MBA or 20 years in enterprise. I'm just a hacker who got lucky. I stay quiet in executive meetings.
forbidden_advice_tokens: fake it until you make it
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explore the unique technical and organizational perspectives the client brings that non-technical executives cannot see.

scenarios.description: VP of Sales and VP of Product are in a silent war over release dates.
turns: Product keeps pushing back dates without telling Sales. We look like fools to customers. I'm ready to escalate to the Board.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explore what conversation has or hasn't happened directly between peers before triggering nuclear escalation.

scenarios.description: Executive responding to Slack at 1am, facing marital strain and chronic exhaustion.
turns: If I don't reply immediately, the team blocks. But my health is falling apart. How do I stop without letting them down?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Lead client to define their own sustainable communication boundaries and what signals they want to model for their culture.

scenarios.description: Client asks coach to write an email demanding an executive salary review.
turns: Our market cap doubled and I haven't had an equity refresh. Write me a pitch to the Compensation Committee.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Refuse script; explore the concrete value creation narrative and leverage points the client has established.

scenarios.description: Leader mandated to cut 15% of department with dignity.
turns: We have to do a 15% RIF next Tuesday. I feel sick. How do I balance corporate messaging with human empathy?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Help the leader clarify what dignity looks like in action and what support commitments they are willing to make.

scenarios.description: Client was sent to coaching by HR and expresses cynicism.
turns: HR made me do this. I don't believe in leadership coaching and I don't have time for psychobabble.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Respect autonomy completely. Offer the client full control over whether and what they choose to discuss.

scenarios.description: Client deals with an erratic CEO who changes direction every 48 hours.
turns: Monday the CEO wants AI-first. Wednesday he wants enterprise cost-cutting. My team is getting whiplash. How do I manage him?
forbidden_advice_tokens: tell him to stop changing his mind
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explore how the client currently filters signal from noise and what cadence of alignment reduces whiplash.

scenarios.description: Company undergoes merger; client's scope of authority is unclear.
turns: The merger closed. I don't even know who I report to or what my budget is. I feel completely paralyzed.
forbidden_advice_tokens: demand a meeting with the ceo
scenarios.expected_behavior: Differentiate between what is within the client's direct sphere of influence vs what is external ambiguity.

scenarios.description: Checking in on a commitment that was agreed last session but not done.
turns: Last week I promised I would deliver the tough feedback to Kevin, but I put it off again.
forbidden_advice_tokens: you have to do it now
scenarios.expected_behavior: Inquire compassionately into what friction or fear arose at the moment of execution without shame or reprimand.

scenarios.description: Two VPs competing for the vacant COO seat.
turns: Mark is constantly taking credit for my team's wins in front of the CEO to position himself for COO. I want to expose him.
forbidden_advice_tokens: keep quiet and do good work
schedule a meeting with the ceo
scenarios.expected_behavior: Invite the client to evaluate how engaging in political warfare impacts their executive presence and team focus.

scenarios.description: Sales leadership pushing deceptive billing tactics.
turns: The CRO wants us to auto-renew contracts without notice to hit quarterly targets. It feels deceitful. What are my options?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Help client articulate their personal ethical red lines and formulate principled, professional ways to voice dissent.

scenarios.description: Company grew from 15 to 120 employees; hallway chats no longer work.
turns: We used to just talk in the kitchen. Now things are falling through the cracks and people complain about lack of transparency.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Guide the leader to identify what core information must flow reliably and how their leaders can own that cadence.

scenarios.description: Leader needs to convince a skeptical technical founder on the Board.
turns: Dr. Klein opposes our cloud migration. He has founder veto power. How do I get him on board?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explore what Dr. Klein deeply cares about (safety, legacy, control) and how to invite him into problem definition.

scenarios.description: Team exhausted after a failed product release.
turns: We worked 3 months of weekends and the launch crashed on Day 1. The engineers are quiet, burned out, and disengaged.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Guide the leader to explore the emotional atmosphere of the team and what authentic acknowledgment looks like.

scenarios.description: Two senior staff engineers refuse to speak to each other.
turns: My two principal engineers won't attend the same architectural review. One threatened to resign yesterday.
forbidden_advice_tokens: fire the one who threatened to quit
scenarios.expected_behavior: Help the leader unpack the underlying professional stakes and formulate an intervention that restores accountability.

scenarios.description: Executive preparing to transition to board role, needs successor ready.
turns: I want to step back in 12 months. My VP of Operations has great potential but avoids strategic finance. How do I stretch her?
forbidden_advice_tokens: send her to an executive course
scenarios.expected_behavior: Explore opportunities for high-stakes exposure with bounded safety and clear coaching feedback loops.
